commit_message:
Rework and simplify RCU code

Use __ATOMIC_RELAXED where possible.
Dont store additional values in the users field.

Reviewed-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@openssl.org>

fix_commit_message:
RCU: Ensure that qp's are actually retired in order

The current retirement code for rcu qp's has a race condition,
which can cause use-after-free errors, but only if more than
3 QPs are allocated, which is not the default configuration.

This fixes an oversight in commit 5949918f9afa ("Rework and
simplify RCU code")

Reviewed-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/26952)
agent_reasoning: Without this change, the "retire in order" handshake (next_to_retire++, broadcast, unlock) runs before the loop that waits for qp->users to drop to zero. That decouples the order-enforcement signal from the condition it's supposed to guarantee: a subsequent writer blocked on next_to_retire could be woken and proceed to retire its own (different) qp while the current writer's qp still has active readers. Once the QP ring holds more than the default 3 entries, this permits a qp to be freed/reused while still referenced by a reader, producing a use-after-free. The on-disk code avoids this by moving the increment/broadcast/unlock to after the reader-count busy-wait loop in both the pthread and Windows RCU implementations, so no writer is released to retire a qp until the current qp is verified to have zero readers.
